results: PASS: the running launcher replaced itself: TexasRevolution.exe now hashes as the v2 build, the v1 build renamed to .old while it ran.
PASS: the game and release.txt moved to v2 with the launcher, and data\classroom.json is byte-for-byte untouched.
PASS: the next launch deletes the renamed old launcher.
PASS: an update that fails part way (server\ held open, after the launcher, public\ and release.txt were already swapped) rolls all of it back: v2 launcher, v2 game, v2 stamp.
PASS: a launch that finds an interrupted swap puts the previous build back before doing anything else.
PASS: an update archive with no launcher in it (every release before this one) updates the game and keeps the launcher.
note: Stand-in games, local setup programs built from this working copy; nothing downloaded from GitHub. Proves the swap and rollback, not the download or a real release.
injections: R1 Apply does not roll back on failure: 3 PASS, then stopped at "A failed update left a different launcher installed"
R2 CleanUp deletes no old launcher (sync and background removed): 2 PASS, then stopped at "The next launch did not delete the old launcher"
R3 CleanUp ignores the swap marker: 4 PASS, then stopped at "A launch after an interrupted swap did not put the old build back"
R4 Apply never swaps the launcher: 0 PASS, stopped at "The installed launcher was not replaced by the v2 launcher"
priorInstalls: Launchers installed before this change download only the update archive and cannot replace themselves; the release that ships this must be installed with TexasRevolutionSetup.exe once.
